title: Plain entry surfaces and precise selection moves
summary: Remove animated grid backgrounds from entry surfaces, move only colored pixels in selections, and make starting palettes optional or custom.

questions.question: When moving a selection containing transparent cells, should the operation cut colored pixels or copy them?
questions.answer: Use option 1: cut-and-move colored pixels only.
questions.decision: Move only non-transparent pixels, clear those colored source pixels, and preserve transparent holes so they never erase destination content.

questions.question: What should Skip starting palette create across color modes?
questions.decision: RGBA and greyscale projects may retain an empty palette; indexed projects also begin empty and add valid colors as they are first used, up to the 256-color limit, rather than silently falling back to a preset.

questions.question: How plain should the three entry surfaces be?
questions.answer: A: remove the grid motif and animated grid only.
questions.decision: Retain subtle non-grid lighting/gradient accents and foreground cards.

questions.question: Should transparent-safe behavior cover selection resize and rotation?
questions.decision: Transform only colored samples; transparent cells never clear or paint pixels, while the selection mask and handles remain usable.

questions.question: Should Custom allow an empty palette?
questions.decision: Custom may be submitted empty and colors can be added later.

questions.question: Does the clarified design tree reflect the shared understanding?
questions.decision: The requirements are approved for specification finalization.

risks: Filtering transparent samples too early could collapse selection bounds, handles, or rotation centers around colored artwork.
Clearing and writing overlapping selections in the wrong order could smear pixels or erase destination artwork under transparent holes.
All-transparent or unchanged gestures could create misleading history and dirty-state entries.
Editor and assistant indexed-color rules could diverge or exceed the 256-color project limit.
Explicit empty palettes could be silently repopulated by project defaults or leave indexed drawing unusable.
Greyscale starting palettes could retain misleading colored values instead of normalized greyscale entries.
Broad CSS cleanup could remove useful non-grid lighting, document transparency checkers, or responsive hierarchy.
Additional launcher choices and empty states could overflow phone/tablet layouts or reduce touch target sizes.
Selection corrections could regress high-pixel-count performance if they add snapshots or full-canvas work during pointer movement.
validation: Unit-test colored-only selection capture/application, transparent destination preservation, overlap, clipping, empty masks, and unchanged results.
Unit-test omitted versus explicit empty palettes, greyscale normalization, indexed registration/deduplication, 256-color fallback, and assistant parity.
Playwright-test rectangular and lasso move/resize/rotate with transparent holes plus exact one-step undo/redo restoration.
Playwright-test Preset, empty Custom, and Skip project creation, honest summaries/hints, indexed first-use growth, and custom design-system color picker behavior.
Review desktop, phone, and tablet splash/auth/Home/launcher screenshots and assert decorative entry grids are absent without removing approved lighting or transparency checkers.
Run studio lint, typecheck, unit tests, production build, focused/full Playwright, changed-file formatting, spec validation, and git diff checks.
